Thanks again for taking the call today, Jordan — really appreciate the time. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can put together a clean cost estimate: 

- Summary from call: Acme Health will run a mix of user-facing summaries and backend enrichment. You estimated roughly 20M–50M generated tokens/month initially, potentially ramping to ~200M over 12 months. CPU/throughput sensitivity: you care about tokens/sec and tail latency.

Questions for you (to confirm):
1) When you say "requests", are you measuring API calls (i.e., HTTP calls per end-user action) or unique prompts?
2) You mentioned tracking characters on your side — can you share an example prompt + response in characters so we can map to tokens?
3) Do you expect to benefit from prompt caching (same system prompts + user variables) for a large share of requests? If so, roughly what % would be cached (your guesstimate is fine).

Why I ask: Redwood bills on tokens. Many customers initially think in characters or "requests"; mapping lets us show unit economics and target $/1M tokens. Prompt caching can reduce billed tokens via prefix caching, but caching eligibility depends on prompt variability and session behavior.

Attached: quick pricing one-pager and a blank mutual action plan — I can fill the MAP once you confirm the answers above and a target $/1M tokens you’re comfortable with.

Next steps: if you can reply with a sample prompt/response (or a CSV of a few rows), Ben and I will run a conversion and draft a 3‑tier estimate (current, near-term ramp, scale).

Best,

2) Characters: here's a quick example from our logs (avg user message):

Thanks for the quick answers, Jordan — super helpful. I converted your example characters into tokens and sketched out unit-econ scenarios below so you can see how we map to $/1M tokens.

Quick primer: "tokens" are the billing unit. Rough rule-of-thumb: 1 token ~= 3–4 characters for typical English text, but it depends on tokenization and whitespace. We'll run your actual samples through the tokenizer for an exact mapping.

Your example mapping (estimate):
- Prompt: 450 characters -> ~120 tokens
- Response: 1,800 characters -> ~450 tokens
- Total per request: ~570 tokens

If 20M tokens/month (generated+billed) vs 50M, here's quick economics at illustrative $/1M tokens: 
- At $20/1M tokens -> 20M = $400; 50M = $1,000; 200M = $4,000
- At $200/1M tokens -> 20M = $4,000; 50M = $10,000; 200M = $40,000

So when you say target $10k/month, that maps to roughly $200/1M tokens at 50M tokens or $50/1M tokens at 200M tokens. We can create a blended plan for ramp scenarios.

Prompt caching impact: if ~35% of your calls are eligible for prefix caching, billed tokens drop proportional to the cached prefix size. Example: if your prompts have a 300-token reusable prefix and 270-token variable + response, caching could reduce billed tokens per hit from ~570 to ~270 (only billed for variable+response), effectively halving cost for cached calls. We'll validate with your samples.

Next steps I propose:
- You share 10–20 sample prompt+response pairs (or CSV) -> Ben will run tokenizer and caching simulation.
- We'll return a 3-scenario cost sheet (20M/50M/200M) with suggested target $/1M and recommended caching/quantization levers.
- If that looks good, we can lock in an intro pricing piece for POC and a mutual action plan fill.

I attached a one-pager and a MAP template in the previous email — happy to pre-fill the MAP with dates and owners once we have the samples.

Want to get a quick 30-min call tomorrow to align on the sample export? Ben is available at 10:30–11:30 PT.

Thanks,
Marissa
